product_scope: The practical service choices split into food-specific recognition/nutrition platforms, general multimodal LLM APIs, generic computer vision, and a first-party nutrition database. Food-specific services reduce integration work; generic VLMs are flexible but require stronger validation and nutrition grounding.
supported_platforms: Cloud APIs can serve both iOS and Android through a backend. Local runtime alternatives are covered in the on-device item.
pricing: Passio Nutrition-AI Hub: Starter $99/month with 1M tokens and $25/1M refill; Growth $599/month with 5M and $10/1M; Pro $2,999/month with 100M and $2.50/1M. Passio says one photo analysis consumes roughly 20k-30k tokens, implying a derived refill-only estimate of $0.05-$0.075/photo at Pro rates, $0.20-$0.30 at Growth, and $0.50-$0.75 at Starter; fixed plan fees and included credits change effective cost. LogMeal uses credits: food recognition plus portion estimation is 1 call/credit and nutrition/recipe data add no credit; a 30-day/200-query/5-user trial is public, while the exact plan table was not visible without account context. Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is $0.25/M input image tokens and $1.50/M output; OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini is $0.75/M input and $4.50/M output with image input billed by image tokens. AWS Rekognition generic DetectLabels starts at $0.001/image for the first million, but is not nutrition-specific. Sources: https://www.passio.ai/pricing, https://logmeal.com/api/pricing/, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-mini, https://aws.amazon.com/rekognition/pricing/
popularity_signal: Passio and LogMeal have public developer/API documentation; popularity or market share is not a reliable proxy for food-photo accuracy.
recognition_behavior: A sensible cloud call returns structured candidate foods, visible ingredients, portion range, confidence, ambiguity flags, and provenance IDs. Nutrition values should be resolved through a canonical database rather than generated as free text.
identified_services: Passio is the strongest directly food-specific option with public mobile SDKs, food database, portion endpoints, and a public MFP partnership claim. LogMeal is another food-specific recognition/portion/nutrition API. Gemini/OpenAI provide flexible multimodal reasoning but do not by themselves guarantee a food taxonomy or nutrition database.
model_or_provider_confidence: Food-specific service capabilities and public prices are high-confidence from vendor documentation; per-photo cost estimates are derived from token/credit assumptions and must be confirmed in a vendor quote.
local_inference_evidence: Cloud services are appropriate for difficult/ambiguous cases; local classifiers can remove obvious non-food/blurred frames and reduce cloud volume. Passio documents both remote photo mode and legacy bundled local models.
portion_and_nutrition_method: Passio/LogMeal expose food-specific nutrition and portion functionality. Generic VLMs require a separate food database, unit conversion, recipe/brand resolution, and user confirmation. No API should be treated as a scale from one RGB photo.
artifact_source: Pricing and limits were checked against official vendor pages on 2026-07-26; consumer APK artifacts are documented in Public_Android_artifact_static_analysis.json.
static_findings: No consumer app's public base XAPK was found to embed an obvious generic VLM or food model. This supports a cloud/service boundary or runtime delivery but does not prove it.
reverse_engineering_limits: Vendor pricing can change, usage tokens are not equivalent across services, and public app artifacts do not reveal private enterprise contracts. Do not infer a consumer app's provider price from public list prices.
candidate_models: For cloud fallback benchmark Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite and OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini against Passio/LogMeal. For local candidates benchmark Gemma 3n E2B, SmolVLM-256M/500M, Apple Foundation Models, and a dedicated food classifier.
mobile_runtime_support: Use a backend abstraction so mobile clients are independent of provider SDKs. Keep local preprocessing in Core ML/LiteRT/ONNX Runtime and send only the minimal image/metadata needed for ambiguous cases.
device_requirements: Cloud models shift cost/latency/privacy to the backend; local models shift cost to app size, memory, thermal load, and device fragmentation. Measure both paths on a fixed device matrix.
expected_food_inference_quality: Food-specific APIs should win on taxonomy/database grounding; general VLMs may win on novel recipes and multilingual descriptions. Both need a benchmark with weighed meals and user correction.
unit_cost_estimate: Derived examples: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite at 1,120 image tokens plus 300 output tokens is roughly $0.00073/photo at listed standard rates; OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini cost depends on its image-tokenization path and output. Passio list-price refill estimate is $0.05-$0.75/photo depending on tier, plus fixed subscription. These are illustrative, not vendor quotes.
privacy_and_compliance: Require DPA/subprocessor list, image retention/deletion guarantees, no training on user photos by default, regional processing, encryption, auditability, and a user-visible cloud consent switch. Food photos can reveal health and household data.
recommendation: For MVP, run Passio and LogMeal trials in parallel with one generic VLM fallback, but keep the product contract centered on user confirmation and deterministic nutrition lookup. Choose by measured corrected-meal accuracy, not raw model-demo quality or lowest token price.
